doc.citation: Le Hérissé, A., Paris, F. & Steemans, P. 2013. Late Ordovician–earliest Silurian palynomorphs from northern Chad and correlation with contemporaneous deposits of southeastern Libya. Bulletin of Geosciences 88(3), 483–504.
doc.comment: The shared Moussegouda cryptospore list and explicitly localised specimens are recorded separately; these overlapping records must not be counted as independent assemblages. Figure 10 mentions southeastern Libya in its heading, but every listed specimen is from Moussegouda. KW-2 has no named spore list. Moussegouda material includes slides previously studied by Calandra (SNEAP internal report, 1964). Reworking concerns marine palynomorphs; spores are not identified as reworked. Velatitetras rugosa has inconsistent authorities in the text and caption. The supplied DOI matches the paper; live Crossref verification was unavailable.

items.age_as_reported: Late Ordovician and possibly earliest Silurian
items.age_basis_detail: Independent marine evidence assigns cores 10–9 to the Hirnantian and cores 2–8 to the latest Hirnantian, with earliest Rhuddanian not excluded. Spores indicate Sub-zone β of the Imperfectotriletes Interval Biozone, whose maximum range is reported as Hirnantian to early Aeronian, probably not younger than Rhuddanian.
items.setting_as_reported: periglacial conditions for cores 9 and 10 and with littoral to marginal marine environmental conditions, with freshwater influences, for the cores 2 to 8 interval
items.notes: Cryptospores are abundant and well preserved; the paper states that the studied miospore assemblages are very similar and supplies this shared list. Twenty-three Moussegouda samples were studied overall, but the number represented by this spore-bearing interval is not specified. Cores 9–10 were preliminarily referred to the Memouniat Formation; the overlying succession is referred to the Tanezzuft Formation. Enclosed cryptospores are highly abundant and Imperfectotriletes numerous at assemblage level. L. divellomedia is absent. Sample-specific illustrated occurrences and the two trilete-bearing samples are separate overlapping records below. Marine palynomorphs receive extensive treatment; reworking is discussed for acritarchs and chitinozoans, not spores.

items.age_basis_detail: Assigned with the succession tentatively referred to the lower Tanezzuft Formation, rather than dated by fossils from this barren core.
items.notes: Micaceous siltstones explicitly reported to produce no palynomorphs, hence no spores. Core 1 was initially grouped with cores 2–8 as Silurian Tanezzuft and Akakkus formations; the later interpretation tentatively places cores 1–8 in the lower Tanezzuft Formation. The overlying unsampled 0–65 m sandy interval is not included.

items.age_basis_detail: Chitinozoans correlate the basal KW-2 assemblage with Moussegouda Assemblage 2. Normalograptus medius from other KW-2 cores ranges across the Ordovician–Silurian boundary and does not provide a definitive boundary assignment.
items.setting_as_reported: nearshore conditions, with obvious fresh water influences
items.notes: The abstract includes two KW-2 samples in the investigated cryptospore-bearing palynomorph material, and the palaeoenvironmental discussion mentions good representation of miospores. No spore taxon or spore-specific sample depth is explicitly assigned to KW-2, so occurrences are empty rather than inferred from Moussegouda. Marine specimens are illustrated from 34–36 m and 36 m, but these depths are not explicitly linked to spores. Figure 10 lists no Libyan specimen despite its heading. The paper re-evaluates marine assemblages previously reported by Grignani, Lanzoni & Elatrash (1991), Palaeozoic and Mesozoic Subsurface Palynostratigraphy in Al Kufrah Basin, Libya.
